breakdown.description: The prompt treats the internal axial force as uniform along the entire bar, even though point loads make the axial force piecewise constant with jumps at the loading points.
breakdown.reason: The Agent failed to resolve this inconsistency. The ground truth corrects the prompt by removing the incorrect instruction to treat the internal force as uniform. The generated specification, however, explicitly follows this incorrect instruction, stating: 'The internal axial force is uniform throughout the entire bar... The internal axial force in each segment (AB, BC, and CD) is 13000 N (tension).'

breakdown.description: The prompt reduces the problem to one net-load stress state, which conflicts with the need to resolve different internal forces and displacements segment by segment.
breakdown.reason: The Agent failed to resolve this inconsistency. The ground truth removes the flawed instruction, thereby requiring a segment-by-segment analysis. The generated specification does the opposite; it follows the flawed instruction and reduces the problem to a single net-load stress state, calculating only one stress value for all segments: 'The normal stress in each segment is σ = F/A = 13000 N / 500 mm² = 26 MPa.'
